Dialogue chain: Meera explains Welbuk Health. Ravi's 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' answers it as a check question. Meera's 'That's the idea.' answers Ravi, and her 'Let's walk through...' leads into 07-4, where he leaves reassured. No reply is skipped and no pronoun lacks a referent.

First-reader concern, no time or place cue from page 6 to page 7: acceptable. In page-07.png, 07-1 shows the reception desk with the monitor, the keyboard and the waiting chairs with seated patients behind. This is the reception already shown on pages 3-4. Ravi's bag is back on his shoulder, while it was on the floor beside his chair in 06-2. Meera, the receptionist from pages 1, 3 and 4, is behind the desk. A reader of pages 1-6 sees the move to reception without a caption, and the source has none.

First-reader concern, the WELBUK HEALTH label touches the left frame: acceptable. The label is set at x:0 on purpose as a tab on the frame. In page-07.png the text still has its inner padding, and the box edge simply lies on the frame. Page 9 uses the same tab style for WELBUK VISION.

First-reader concern, the 'ravi' label crosses the right border of 07-3: this is a placeholder artefact. The speaker is kind:head at 970,760. In page-07.png Ravi is the over-the-shoulder back of a head and a hand holding the phone, cut by the right frame on purpose.

First-reader concern, the 'anany' label is clipped by the meera box in 07-4: this is a placeholder artefact. In page-07.png Ananya, in white coat and stethoscope, and Meera, in blue kurta with braid, stand apart in the glass doorway, both waving. They do not overlap.

First-reader concern, Ravi's tail in 07-2 is only a small notch: acceptable. In page-07.png the short tail comes off the balloon's lower right toward Ravi's face, and he is the only person in the panel.

readingReview.comparison: The first reader's natural order is 07-1 Meera, then 07-2 Ravi's question and the label, then 07-3 Meera, then the 07-4 caption. This is the intended order, and the first reader found no skipped reply. The first reader raised five other concerns: the missing page 6 to 7 cue, the label on the frame, the ravi label crossing the frame, the clipped 'anany' label and the small tail. All five are resolved above with evidence from the art. The cue is visual, through the reception setting and the bag back on Ravi's shoulder. The others are a deliberate tab placement or placeholder artefacts that do not appear in page-07.png. No differences remain.
observations: In the unnumbered PNG there is one balloon per panel in 07-1 and 07-3, so no two nearby balloons can be confused. In 07-2 the question balloon is at the top left and the teal label below it, so the question is read first, and the label works as a product tag for the phone.

The middle row is read 07-2 (left, 560 wide) and then 07-3 (right). Meera's answer balloon sits at the top of 07-3 at the same height as Ravi's question, so the question and answer read as one horizontal exchange.

In page-07.png, Meera's gaze and pointing hand go toward Ravi's phone, and Ravi looks at it, which leads into 07-2. In 07-2 Ravi looks up to screen right toward 07-3, where Meera faces right toward him. In 07-4 Ravi waves back toward the doorway at left, so the panel ends with him walking off to the right toward the page turn.

transitions.observation: page-06.png ends in the consultation room: Ananya says the next-steps line, the PLAN OF CARE screen is visible, and the bag is on the floor. In 07-1 the reception desk, the waiting area and Meera are shown, and the bag is back on Ravi's shoulder. The place change after the consultation is clear from the art.

In 07-1 Meera points at the phone in Ravi's right hand. In 07-2 he holds the same dark-blue phone in both hands with the screen toward the reader (calendar and heart icons) and asks his question. The prop and the action carry over.

Ravi's question is answered by Meera's 'That's the idea.' Ravi is seen from behind on the right holding the phone, and Meera's open hand gestures toward it. The left/right placement from 07-1 is kept.

The offer of a walkthrough is followed by the departure outside the clinic entrance. Ravi waves with his right hand and holds the phone in his left, with the bag on his shoulder, while Ananya and Meera wave from the doorway. The 'smoother visit' caption closes the visit.

Ravi walks off to the right, and the page turns. Page 8 opens with 'Meanwhile, the pharmacy is notified...'. In the current page-08.svg and page-08.png the pharmacist packs a bag beside a tablet showing a pill card. Pages 1-7 have shown the clinic and 06-2 lists intelligent prescribing and labs under PLAN OF CARE, so 'Meanwhile' reads as during or just after Ravi's visit. Limitation: the page-08 storyboard PNGs are stale (see the page 08 response). I judged this transition against the current page-08 SVG and the composed page-08.png.

workflow/review/page-08.png does match the current SVG positions listed above, so the art and lettering preview is current.

Script vs source: every caption, label and the lab technician's line match PAGE 8 in original.txt word for word. The six beats follow Request 4 in order: pharmacy notified and filling; lab notified; samples at the clinic lab the same day; Ravi notified by app, email or WhatsApp; the doctor on Welbuk Care; the clinic on Welbuk Practice. No drug, test, value or diagnosis appears in the text or on the screens in 08-1 to 08-6. The screens show only a pill card, test-tube icons and check marks.

Art vs script, from the panel PNGs and the preview. 08-1: the pharmacist (moustache, grey temples, white coat over a blue shirt) puts a plain box into a paper bag with his right hand while holding the bag with his left, next to a tablet on a stand showing a pill card. 08-2: the lab technician (high bun, round glasses, freckles, purple gloves) holds a capped tube and looks at the monitor, which shows three tube icons. 08-3: Ravi sits in the collection chair with his bag on his lap, pressing cotton to the inside of his left elbow with his right hand, watch on his left wrist, and smiles at the lab technician. She is labelling a red-capped tube and speaks toward him. 08-4: Ravi on a sofa at dusk, phone in his right hand showing a check card with app, envelope and chat icons, watch on his left wrist. 08-5: Ananya at her desk, holding the tablet in both hands, with tube and check icons, stethoscope, window and plant. 08-6: Meera (braid, bangle on her right hand on the mouse) smiles at a monitor turned toward the reader, which shows a check card.

First-reader concern, 'Meanwhile' with no clear referent: acceptable when read in sequence. Page 6 (06-2) shows PLAN OF CARE: intelligent prescribing · labs, and page 7 ends with Ravi leaving the clinic. 'Meanwhile' then reads as during or just after the visit, and the 08-1 tablet shows a pill card for the prescription.

First-reader concern, who sends the notifications: acceptable. Pages 2 and 5-7 set up Welbuk Practice, Welbuk Care and Welbuk Health. The device screens and the product names in 08-5 and 08-6 attribute the notifications to the Welbuk system. The passive 'is notified' is the user's own wording in Request 4.

First-reader concern, Meera appears without introduction in 08-6: acceptable. Meera is introduced on pages 1, 3 and 7 and is drawn on-model in 08-6 with her braid, blue kurta and bangle at the reception desk.
First-reader concern, Ravi has no visible reaction to 'All done, Ravi!': resolved by the art. In 08-3 Ravi smiles toward the lab technician while pressing the cotton pad, and she speaks toward him.
First-reader concern, the empty tall panel 08-4: resolved by the art. The window at sunset, the curtain, the sofa and Ravi fill the panel.

First-reader concern, the time jump from 'Later that day' to 'Results ready': acceptable. The location changes to Ravi's home and the caption opens with the state 'Results ready:'. The comic makes no claim about turnaround, so it does not need to give an exact interval. Note that the dusk light could be read as the same evening. The source's 'Some days later' is a stage direction, not caption text.

First-reader concern, 'notified' five times: acceptable. It is a deliberate parallel structure taken from the user's own 'gets notified' phrasing in Request 4. The art changes in every panel: pharmacy, lab, collection, home, consultation desk, reception.

First-reader concern, NEW PRESCRIPTION is far from the pharmacist and not tied to a device: largely resolved in the preview. The label at 30,316 now covers the tablet itself, with only its top bezel visible above the label, so it reads as the tablet's screen text. The cost is that the drawn pill card is hidden. The 08-6 label overlaps the top of the monitor, and the 08-5 label sits right beside the tablet. The 08-2 label is above the monitor, near it but not on it. Acceptable.
First-reader concern, text touching box edges: most cases were storyboard font artefacts, but two still appear to touch in the preview (see issues).

readingReview.comparison: The recorded first reading follows the intended panel and dialogue order. Its continuity, identity and repetition concerns are judged acceptable above, with evidence from pages 1-7 and the art. However, that reading was made on a PNG that no longer matches the current SVG and script: the captions, balloon and labels in 08-1 to 08-6 were moved and re-broken. So it cannot stand as the first reading for this request. The predicted order below is my own reading of the current SVG and the composed page-08.png. It is not a replacement for the required new image-only first reading.
observations: In page-08.png, 08-3 has the caption at the top left and the balloon at the far right, with its tail down to the lab technician's mouth. There is only one speaker, so the balloon cannot be misattributed.

In 08-2 the caption and label are stacked at the top right above the monitor, and the lab technician's gaze goes right toward the monitor. Reading caption, then label, then the gaze leads out to the right edge, which is correct.
In the bottom tier, the caption row across 08-4 and 08-5 is the proximity risk listed in the issues.

transitions.observation: Page turn after Ravi leaves, then 'Meanwhile' at the pharmacy, with a pill card on the tablet tying it to the 06-2 plan of care. Acceptable.
Parallel order receipt: 'The lab is notified.' and the lab technician picks up an empty tube by the monitor's order card. Acceptable.
The caption 'Later that day' and the same lab (blue collection chair, tube rack, monitor with tube icons) show Ravi returning after he left in 07-4. Acceptable.

'We'll let you know when your results are ready' is paid off by 'Results ready: Ravi is notified.' at home, with a check card on his phone. The promise and its payoff are clear. The interval is not stated (see observations).
The same check-mark card appears on Ananya's tablet. The parallel structure is clear, but see the caption-row proximity issue.
The same check card appears on the reception monitor, with Meera on-model. This completes the patient, doctor and clinic sequence from Request 4.
From the present-day notification to 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' with Ravi on a train. The conditional caption and the train setting mark the shift to the future. Acceptable.

All are resolved above with evidence from the source and page-09.png. No differences remain.
